reason: offer (mcp-re-proxy/src/audit_sink/mod.rs:168-183) now calls reserve_slot (mod.rs:149-157), which does the ceiling test and the increment in one fetch_update, so concurrent callers cannot all see the same sub-ceiling value. concurrent_offers_at_the_ceiling_admit_only_the_remaining_slots (mod.rs:437-477) runs 16 barrier-started contenders 300 times through the real offer function and asserts depth == ceiling and 15 drops. Both limbs are closed: the race, and a single-threaded test that could not detect it.

Ledger 06b9b2637b0f75b9 (status fixed, verdict confirmed) quotes the same two lines this row describes: the `if let Ok` no-op record and the `unwrap_or_default` records. Its smallest_fix is the guard recovery now at mcp-re-proxy/src/audit_sink/mod.rs:208-211, used by both records (:214-216) and record (:220-222). a_poisoned_collector_still_records_and_reports_what_it_holds (mod.rs:263-287) poisons the lock for real and asserts 2 records. Both limbs are covered: silent discard, and empty read as 'nothing recorded'.

Wrap limb: the reservation happens before try_send (mcp-re-proxy/src/audit_sink/mod.rs:175-179), so the writer can never dequeue a line whose increment has not happened. The writer decrements with checked_sub (writer.rs:141-142), and the failure release at mod.rs:180 undoes only the offer's own reservation for a line that was never received. an_unpaired_line_does_not_wrap_the_occupancy_counter (writer.rs:348-355) drives write_until_disconnected with queued=0. Check-then-act limb: reserve_slot is one atomic step (mod.rs:149-157), and concurrent_offers_at_the_ceiling_admit_only_the_remaining_slots (mod.rs:437-477) witnesses it. Attributed records can now be dropped only on a disconnected channel or a genuinely full depth.
missed_residue: Different cause, info-level, recorded only so the wording limb is not lost: report_drops always says 'the audit hand-off queue was full' (mcp-re-proxy/src/audit_sink/writer.rs:183-187). That text is also emitted for unattributed records refused at STDERR_AUDIT_UNATTRIBUTED_CEILING (mod.rs:104, 175-177), when the queue is only at 3/4 depth. The drop cause is still misdescribed for that class, though no longer for a queue that is empty.

reason: flush_stderr_audit is gone. app::run (mcp-re-proxy/src/app.rs:143-160) calls crate::audit_sink::drain::at_shutdown at :158 after validation+serving on every return route, and main.rs:58 enters only through app::run. at_shutdown (drain.rs:56-64) retries a Full queue up to the 2s bound (drain.rs:25, 122-140). It reports Drained, or OutcomeUnknown plus unreported drops (drain.rs:147-182), so a loaded shutdown no longer ends the stream silently. The child-process test a_record_enqueued_immediately_before_teardown_still_reaches_stderr (app.rs:893-960) exits right after run returns and asserts that seq=1999 reached stderr. It also guards against a zero-test child run (app.rs:943-948). The OOM/SIGKILL/panic-unwind modes cannot be drained by any in-process design, and the seq-restart limb is tracked as still-present 28fe5fccf0545602.

Ledger 66ab4b10047ef26c (fixed, 38d283bc #883) has the same title and subject: a discarded spawn result with the sender installed anyway. At HEAD, writer.rs:85-109 keeps the spawn result. On Err it latches STDERR_AUDIT_WRITES_FAILED and eprintln's a WARNING that no record will reach stderr. The disconnected channel makes drain_queue return OutcomeUnknown via enqueue_flush's Disconnected arm (drain.rs:105-106, 132). at_shutdown then prints the unreported drop count (drain.rs:60, 173-182). The row's 'zero records, no error anywhere' limb and its 'eprintln the spawn error' remedy are both met.

Every limb is closed at HEAD, but the cited later finding is narrower. Ledger 7628fcc8213a594a adjudicates only the accounting asymmetry: Flush took no reservation, so at full line occupancy it could not be enqueued. It does not cover this row's 'no caller of the flush' limb or its 'seq gap with no drop line' limb. Its recommended fix (sync_channel DEPTH+1) was not taken: writer.rs:80 is still sync_channel(STDERR_AUDIT_QUEUE_DEPTH), and the full-queue arm is closed instead by enqueue_flush retrying until the bound (drain.rs:122-140). The caller limb is closed by app.rs:158, and the silent-gap limb by the OutcomeUnknown line carrying unreported drops (drain.rs:160-182). This should be recorded as no-longer-present with these citations, with 7628fcc8213a594a as a partial overlap rather than the duplicate root.

A production caller now exists at mcp-re-proxy/src/app.rs:158, on every route out of run (app.rs:156-159). The composition root therefore wires the shutdown drain this row said was missing. The try_send-on-full limb is closed by the retry loop (drain.rs:122-140). The documented loss is now bounded and stated as Drained or OutcomeUnknown (drain.rs:147-171). The rider that 'seq restarts so no visible gap' is still-present 28fe5fccf0545602 in this batch, not lost.

This is the same defect as 66ab4b10047ef26c (fixed). writer.rs:85-109 handles the spawn Err: it sets the latch and prints a WARNING on the diagnostic channel. drain_queue reports OutcomeUnknown (drain.rs:105-106) together with the unreported drop count (drain.rs:60, 173-182). That closes the 'report_drops only on the nonexistent writer, nobody reads the counter' limb. The 'ON posture over a dead sink' limb remains in a weakened form: security_audit_record still prints STDERR unconditionally (serving_capabilities.rs:159-166) because the writer is lazy. It is now followed by an explicit WARNING, which is the remedy the row itself proposes, so it is not a surviving silent defect.

r11 dc9caf7977442bf1 carries this title nearly verbatim and was adjudicated against the same fix as 66ab4b10047ef26c (38d283bc). It records that the type cannot be installed from configuration (AuditSinkKind None/Stderr only) and that pub is needed for the tests in mcp-re-proxy/tests/integration_async. The 'mutex on the request path' limb is not addressed by 086832, but it applies only to a sink now documented as not for deployment, and the lock covers just a push or clone (mod.rs:208-222).

At HEAD report_drops (mcp-re-proxy/src/audit_sink/writer.rs:178-195) puts the count back with fetch_add and latches failed when write_record fails. a_drop_count_survives_a_failed_report_and_is_reported_later (writer.rs:360-384) drives an always-failing writer, asserts the count of 7 is retained, then reports it. The test's 'Vec cannot fail' gap is closed by the Failing writer.

the_verified_context_carrier_is_attached_only_for_a_trusted_inner_channel (mcp-re-proxy/src/serving_capabilities.rs:~489-511) calls the real verified_context_carrier (serving_capabilities.rs:218-238). mcp_transport_contract (mcp-re-proxy/src/serving_capabilities.rs:134-146) takes &McpTransportContractState and derives accepted from state.versions(). It has no OFF arm, no is_empty, and no DeploymentRequest in scope. The positive result holds in stronger form. However, the reconciler's claim that the 'constructible outside the classifier' caveat is gone is only partly true: it has moved, as recorded in missed_residue.
missed_residue: Low, fail-closed, documentation overclaim: config_state::mcp_transport_contract::classify is `pub` (mcp-re-proxy/src/config_state/mod.rs:73, mcp_transport_contract.rs:35-40) and total. It produces a state with an EMPTY versions set from any DeploymentRequest. The doc at mcp_transport_contract.rs:20-22 says 'a state that is held names at least one version', but that holds only because validation runs violations (validation/mod.rs:263) before classify_total (validation/total_machines.rs:38) is used. That makes it call ordering, not a property the value owns (R-SEAL). An empty set yields McpTransportPolicy::mcp_2026_07_28(&[]) with require_protocol_version_header=true (mcp-re-http-profile/src/mcp_transport/mod.rs:73-80), which refuses every request. The consequence is therefore fail-closed, but the doc overstates the seal.

reason: The consumer is demonstrated. mcp-re-proxy/src/app.rs:634-637 builds the policy from the validated state and installs it with verifier_policy.with_mcp_transport, and app.rs:641 installs that VerifierPolicy into the proxy. request_admission.rs:111-125 verifies every request through Verifier::verify_request. That reaches verify::full_request (mcp-re-http-profile/src/verifier.rs:89-104), which calls floor_request first (verify/full/request.rs:43), and the floor runs policy.mcp_transport().enforce(request)? after the signature (verify/floor/request.rs:123-135). The OFF arm no longer exists, and an empty set is refused at validation (config_state/mcp_transport_contract.rs:42-57). The public-precondition weakness is tracked open as b4648cd2c7bb70fc.

The positive confirmation still holds: serving_capabilities.rs:134-146 reads state.versions(), and there is no is_empty, no length test and no re-classification. The deferred 'is it USED' question is answered by app.rs:634-641 -> request_admission.rs:120 -> verify/floor/request.rs:135. The reconciler's phrase 'classify as its only producer' is accurate, but classify does no checking. The same low, fail-closed seal overstatement is recorded under 627e9377606508d9 and is not repeated here.

Consumption is demonstrated by the same chain as 7d557df70ca94ccf (app.rs:634-641; request_admission.rs:111-125; mcp-re-http-profile/src/verify/full/request.rs:43; verify/floor/request.rs:134-135). On the dispatch-by-body-emptiness limb: verify_bodyless_request is defined only at mcp-re-http-profile/src/bodyless/mod.rs:336, and a grep finds no caller in mcp-re-proxy/src. Every proxy request, including a signed POST with an empty body, therefore goes through verify_request and the body-bearing enforce. The weaker bodyless path cannot be selected inside the proxy. Its own weakness is tracked open as aee88e1f0f444c49, and the precondition width as b4648cd2c7bb70fc.
